title: Vesper and the Sigil
premise: Gideon Okafor, a memory-thief bound to a valley where magic cannot follow, is given a dying stranger's map and a debt she never agreed to: recover the soul of a girl sold to the court beneath the mountain before the thirteenth moon turns. Following the map, Gideon discovers that every stolen memory she carries is a fragment of her own forgotten past — that she was once the soul's twin, traded in her place. To reach the court, she must barter with memory-eaters, outwit a magpie-hearted guide, and finally surrender her most precious theft. In the end, Gideon chooses to return the stolen soul at the cost of her own name, walking out of the mountain as someone new: neither thief nor twin, but the author of a self made from what she chooses to remember.
about_author: K. M. Quintana is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction about the things we cannot put down. They write in the high desert, where they claim the light makes forgetting impossible.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet her mid-heist, lifting a widow's grief from a locked memory-jar, establishing the valley's magic-dead rules and her trade. Emotional beat: competent loneliness; she is excellent at taking what others can't hold.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses at the valley's edge where no one ever arrives, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'thirteen turns.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The map won't leave her — it burns when set down, and its ink rearranges into scenes she almost remembers. The valley elders demand she destroy it. Emotional beat: first crack of compulsion and curiosity.

chapters.title: The Widow's Kindness
chapters.summary: Widow Sefu's POV. The woman whose grief Gideon stole finds her instead, offering bread and an old story about twin girls sold beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness that unsettles Gideon more than threats.

chapters.title: Crossing the Rim
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She slips past the wardens at night; the moment she crosses the rim, magic floods back into the world and her stolen memories begin whispering aloud. Emotional beat: vertigo — the world is louder than she is.

chapters.title: The Magpie Road
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, introducing Perrin, a magpie-shifter guide who owes the dead stranger a favor and resents it. He agrees to lead her for one memory of his choosing. Emotional beat: wary banter masking mutual need.

chapters.title: Towns Made of Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. He shows her the outer world: villages lit by bottled memories, where the poor sell their pasts to eat. Gideon recognizes her own jars on a market shelf. Emotional beat: shame curdling into anger.

chapters.title: The First Gate
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The map leads to a toll-bridge guarded by a Ferryman who accepts payment only in memories. Gideon pays with a childhood summer and feels it go. Emotional beat: the true price of the journey becomes real.

chapters.title: Echoes in Her Hands
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Without that summer, she can't remember why she flinches at rivers. Perrin notices her gaps growing. Emotional beat: quiet horror — the journey is erasing her even as it reveals her.

chapters.title: The Memory-Eaters' Market
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A black bazaar where memories are tasted like wine. To learn the court's location, she must let an eater taste one of hers — and he recoils, calling it 'court-stamped.' Emotional beat: revelation; her past is entangled with the enemy.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns, One Spent
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. First moon sets. Perrin confesses the dying stranger was his sister, who stole the map from the court itself. Emotional beat: guilt shared becomes trust.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was Sold
chapters.summary: Interlude, the soul Adaeze's POV inside the mountain. She remembers a twin, a bargain, a mother's tears — but not which sister stayed. Emotional beat: longing without a name to long for.

chapters.title: Wolves of the Second Moon
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Court hunters — hollow-eyed riders who smell stolen goods — ambush them. Gideon survives by feeding a hunter a false memory so vivid it unmakes him. Emotional beat: her gift revealed as a weapon, and it frightens her.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Ash
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In a burned library, a blind archivist reads the map by touch and tells Gideon the truth's shape: two girls, one contract, one soul kept as surety. Emotional beat: the premise cracks open — she may be the trade.

chapters.title: Which Sister Stayed
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She searches her own stolen hoard for proof and finds a sealed jar labeled in her mother's hand. She cannot bring herself to open it. Emotional beat: denial at full strength.

chapters.title: Third Moon, Broken Promise
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Perrin tries to steal the map and abandon her, believing the quest dooms them both; she catches him and, instead of rage, gives him a memory freely. Emotional beat: forgiveness as turning point; alliance becomes friendship.

chapters.title: The Salt Flats Sing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Crossing the flats, the land itself hums with the memories buried there. Gideon hears her mother's voice for the first time since childhood. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through wonder.

chapters.title: Court-Stamped
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The memory-eater from the market finds her again, offers to buy the sealed jar at any price. His hunger confirms what's inside. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by terror.

chapters.title: Halfway Moon
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. In the court, the soul begins to fade as moons pass; the court feeds on her slowly. She starts leaving messages in dreams. Emotional beat: fading hope learning to fight.

chapters.title: Dream Correspondence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Adaeze's dream-messages reach her: images of a kitchen, a lullaby, two pairs of small shoes. Gideon opens the jar at last. Emotional beat: shattering recognition — she is the sister who stayed, and she chose to forget.

chapters.title: The Bargain Replayed
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, mother's POV. The full truth: famine year, the court's offer, a mother who sent one daughter up the mountain road and kept the other — then paid a thief to steal the memory from herself. Emotional beat: devastating compassion; everyone was guilty and grieving.

chapters.title: I Am the Debt
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She understands now: the map wasn't a rescue mission. It was her mother's apology, delivered late. The soul beneath the mountain is her twin, Adaeze. Emotional beat: identity collapse — everything she built herself from was a wall.

chapters.title: Sixth Moon, Empty Hands
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Gideon goes silent and still for days. Perrin, who has lost everyone, refuses to lose her to despair and drags her onward by sheer stubbornness. Emotional beat: friendship as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Rebate
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the bridge again, the Ferryman returns her summer unasked — payment, he says, for a debt he owed her mother. She weeps holding a season she'd sold. Emotional beat: grace from an unexpected quarter.

chapters.title: Approaches to the Mountain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The mountain's approaches: three doors — gold for the rich, iron for the strong, bone for the desperate. Only the bone door opens for those with nothing left to lose. Emotional beat: grim resolve.

chapters.title: Down the Bone Stair
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Descending through the mountain's throat, past galleries of bottled souls, she sees what the court actually is: a vault of purchased selves. Emotional beat: righteous fury replacing fear.

chapters.title: Audience with the Under-Court
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Before the masked court, she claims kinship and demands Adaeze's release. The court laughs: contracts bind both ways, and her name is on the original too. Emotional beat: hubris checked; the trap was always legal.

chapters.title: The Fine Print of Souls
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Reading the contract with a thief's eye, she finds the flaw: the court holds Adaeze's soul, but not her name — names were never sold. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Ninth Moon, The Court's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. The court offers Adaeze eternity as their favorite if she denounces her sister. Adaeze, who barely knows Gideon, refuses anyway. Emotional beat: love as a decision, not a memory.

chapters.title: Thieves' Parliament
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She rallies the market's memory-eaters, the Ferryman, and the archivist — everyone the court has bought from — into a conspiracy of the sold. Emotional beat: the lonely thief becomes the center of a web.

chapters.title: The Great Withdrawal
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. On the new moon, every conspirator demands their memories back at once, overloading the court's ledgers while Gideon slips toward the vault. Emotional beat: collective courage; chaos as cover.

chapters.title: The Vault of Purchased Selves
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Among ten thousand jars she finds Adaeze's — and beside it, a second jar with her own name. The court kept a copy of her all along. Emotional beat: the final choice arrives early and terrible.

chapters.title: Twelfth Moon, What a Name Is Worth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. To break the contract fully, a name must be surrendered to balance the ledger. Gideon signs away 'Gideon Okafor,' emptying herself of the identity she built. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship — she writes herself blank.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Climax, Gideon and Adaeze alternating. As the moon completes its turn, Gideon frees Adaeze; the court unravels as its ledger balances; the sisters flee up the bone stair as the mountain's lights go out behind them. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Two Pairs of Shoes
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. On the mountainside, the sisters meet as strangers who share a lullaby. Adaeze offers her half of everything she remembers. Emotional beat: tentative, trembling reunion.

chapters.title: Rebuilding from Fragments
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Nameless, she reassembles a self from chosen pieces: Perrin's loyalty, the widow's bread, her mother's apology, Adaeze's offered memories. Emotional beat: identity as curation, not inheritance.

chapters.title: The Return Through the Rim
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She crosses back into the magic-dead valley carrying Adaeze, breaking the rule that exiles magic — because the valley cannot follow what refuses to be followed. Emotional beat: home redefined as people, not borders.

chapters.title: Settling Accounts
chapters.summary: Perrin's POV. Perrin buries his sister's map at last and stays in the valley, opening a shop that returns stolen memories free of charge. Emotional beat: mourning completed into purpose.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Epilogue: under a fresh moon, Gideon — keeping the name she rewrote for herself — teaches Adaeze the valley, and the two begin returning what the mountain took. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed; memory as a gift given forward.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Gideon's POV. On the evening star's first appearance, the sisters plant a garden over the old memory-jars. Gideon realizes she no longer needs to steal what she can grow. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — the self, at last, is hers.
